investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod the eval attempted to schedule was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm". The underlying VM-backed peer-pod resource (kata.peerpods.io/vm) is exhausted on the only two nodes that carry it, and the remaining four nodes do not match the required node affinity or selector, leaving no schedulable target for any new remote-agent pod. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the eval runner never produced the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both nodes that expose it. With 0 remaining VM slots and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (line 1885), which triggers pod creation; that pod never transitions out of Pending, so the probe times out after ~131–146 s and returns no evidence, failing all four required-evidence assertions (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 nodes, with no preemption path available.
failed-check.timing: check latencyMs=137371 ms, pod stuck unscheduled for 131 s before the probe gave up — consistent with a scheduling deadlock, not a transient delay.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck 144 s, latencyMs=147679 — same resource exhaustion hit a second independent probe.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck 146 s, latencyMs=153605 — third independent probe hit the same wall.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent because the pod never started and the runner never reached the evidence-writing code path.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the code path that submits the pod requiring kata.peerpods.io/vm.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract at line 256 requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be satisfied when the pod never schedules.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: all three checks (remote-agent-create required, remote-agent-state required, remote-agent-runtime optional) share the same swarm-backed VM provisioning path, explaining why all three fail simultaneously.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — existing remote-agent pods or other workloads are holding all VM slots and have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new allocations.
[Likely] A previous eval run or user-initiated remote agent was not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner may have failed or been interrupted), leaving orphaned pods that continue to hold VM slots.

[Possible] The two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have been cordoned, drained, or reduced in VM quota (e.g., cloud provider VM quota change or node pool scaling event), shrinking available capacity below the concurrent demand.

[Possible] Node affinity or selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec have become more restrictive (or the node labels have changed), reducing the eligible node set from a larger pool to exactly 2 nodes, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.
[Lower likelihood] A cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange for the namespace hosting remote-agent pods is preventing new pod admission even when node capacity exists.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the two kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots, the exhaustion hypothesis is wrong and the cause is elsewhere (e.g., admission webhook rejection, API auth failure, or a runner bug).
If the eval passes immediately after no pods are released or capacity is added, the root cause is not VM exhaustion but a transient scheduler or API error.
If only remote-agent-create fails while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime pass in the same run window, the failure is isolated to the create path rather than shared VM capacity.
If the scheduler message changes to an auth, quota, or webhook error on re-run, the VM exhaustion reading of the current message would be incorrect.

If node affinity labels on the eligible nodes are found to have changed to exclude remote-agent pods entirely (0 matching nodes instead of 2), the cause would be a label/selector misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion on otherwise-eligible nodes.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated across all eligible nodes and fails with a capacity warning before attempting remote-agent pod creation — this would surface exhaustion before the pod scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that verifies the withCleanup path successfully terminates remote-agent pods after each probe run, catching slot leakage from the eval infrastructure itself.
Add a persistent-pod inventory eval that alerts when the count of running pods requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm exceeds a configured high-water mark, providing early warning before full exhaustion.

Consider a remote-agent-capacity check registered in features.json that independently monitors available VM slots on kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, decoupled from the agent creation flow, so capacity degradation is visible even when no new agents are being created.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was stuck Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods timed out before reaching a running state and the eval runner never received the agent identity or state payloads required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource slots across the two eligible nodes. Because the pod could not be scheduled, the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) never returned a live agent, so the probe exited with a failure message and produced no evidence payload. All four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing because the agent creation step — which is the prerequisite for state polling — never completed. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=147679 (~147 s) exceeds the 144 s stuck-pod window reported in the message, confirming the probe waited the full scheduler timeout before failing.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource exhaustion: the two affinity-eligible nodes have no remaining VM slots, and no preemption is possible. All three remote-agent checks show the same scheduler rejection, making this the strongest explanation (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: four of six nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, leaving only two nodes eligible. If the selector was recently tightened or node labels changed, effective capacity would drop even if raw VM slots exist on other nodes.

Tertiary — VM quota or cloud-provider limit: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is backed by a cloud VM quota; if the quota was reached or a billing/quota event occurred, the device plugin would report 0 allocatable slots on both eligible nodes.

Lower confidence — eval runner dependency on remote-agent-create: remote-agent-state calls createAgent internally (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905); if the create step is broken for any reason other than scheduling, state polling would also fail. However, the explicit scheduler message in all three checks points to scheduling as the common cause rather than an application-layer defect.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of any of the three remote-agent checks with a fully populated evidence payload (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) would indicate the scheduling issue was transient and has self-resolved.

Cluster node inspection showing that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero and no pods are consuming it would suggest the scheduler message was a false positive or a device-plugin reporting error rather than true exhaustion.
Evidence that the pod was scheduled and reached Running state but the application layer returned an error would shift the root cause away from VM capacity toward an API or agent runtime defect.
A passing result on remote-agent-create while remote-agent-state still fails would indicate the state-polling logic itself is broken rather than the shared scheduling layer.
Node affinity labels matching all six nodes (not just two) would rule out a label-drift cause and confirm raw VM slot exhaustion as the sole constraint.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API (or a cluster metrics endpoint) for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used counts on each eligible node, alerting before slots reach zero rather than after pod scheduling fails.
Add a pre-flight eval that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available before attempting agent creation, so the failure message is a capacity warning rather than a scheduler timeout.
Add an eval that checks node affinity label consistency across all nodes in the remote-agents scheduling pool to catch label drift before it reduces effective capacity.

Consider a canary eval that creates and immediately destroys a minimal remote agent on a short interval (e.g., every 5 minutes) to detect VM slot exhaustion earlier than the current 20-minute staleAfterMinutes window.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available for scheduling. Because the agent pod never started, the eval runner could not collect any evidence, and all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) is identical across all three checks, indicating the pod never reached a running state on any attempt. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"), so no existing pod could be evicted to free capacity. The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with type "remote" (line 1918), which triggers the pod submission that fails at the infrastructure layer before any application-level response is produced. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval probe runs alongside production workloads.

Lower probability — a recent node or taint change that removed nodes from the eligible pool, shrinking capacity without a corresponding increase in VM slots on remaining nodes (no supporting evidence in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod the eval attempted to schedule was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm". The underlying VM-backed peer-pod resource (kata.peerpods.io/vm) is exhausted on the only two nodes that carry it, and the remaining four nodes do not match the required node affinity or selector, leaving no schedulable target for any new remote-agent pod. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the eval runner never produced the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both nodes that expose it. With 0 remaining VM slots and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (line 1885), which triggers pod creation; that pod never transitions out of Pending, so the probe times out after ~131–146 s and returns no evidence, failing all four required-evidence assertions (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 nodes, with no preemption path available.
failed-check.timing: check latencyMs=137371 ms, pod stuck unscheduled for 131 s before the probe gave up — consistent with a scheduling deadlock, not a transient delay.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck 144 s, latencyMs=147679 — same resource exhaustion hit a second independent probe.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck 146 s, latencyMs=153605 — third independent probe hit the same wall.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent because the pod never started and the runner never reached the evidence-writing code path.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the code path that submits the pod requiring kata.peerpods.io/vm.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract at line 256 requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be satisfied when the pod never schedules.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: all three checks (remote-agent-create required, remote-agent-state required, remote-agent-runtime optional) share the same swarm-backed VM provisioning path, explaining why all three fail simultaneously.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — existing remote-agent pods or other workloads are holding all VM slots and have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new allocations.
[Likely] A previous eval run or user-initiated remote agent was not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner may have failed or been interrupted), leaving orphaned pods that continue to hold VM slots.

[Possible] The two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have been cordoned, drained, or reduced in VM quota (e.g., cloud provider VM quota change or node pool scaling event), shrinking available capacity below the concurrent demand.

[Possible] Node affinity or selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec have become more restrictive (or the node labels have changed), reducing the eligible node set from a larger pool to exactly 2 nodes, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.
[Lower likelihood] A cluster-level resource quota or LimitRange for the namespace hosting remote-agent pods is preventing new pod admission even when node capacity exists.

If the eval passes immediately after no pods are released or capacity is added, the root cause is not VM exhaustion but a transient scheduler or API error.

followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated across all eligible nodes and fails with a capacity warning before attempting remote-agent pod creation — this would surface exhaustion before the pod scheduling timeout.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was stuck Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods timed out before reaching a running state and the eval runner never received the agent identity or state payloads required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource slots across the two eligible nodes. Because the pod could not be scheduled, the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) never returned a live agent, so the probe exited with a failure message and produced no evidence payload. All four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing because the agent creation step — which is the prerequisite for state polling — never completed. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource exhaustion: the two affinity-eligible nodes have no remaining VM slots, and no preemption is possible. All three remote-agent checks show the same scheduler rejection, making this the strongest explanation (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: four of six nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, leaving only two nodes eligible. If the selector was recently tightened or node labels changed, effective capacity would drop even if raw VM slots exist on other nodes.

Tertiary — VM quota or cloud-provider limit: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is backed by a cloud VM quota; if the quota was reached or a billing/quota event occurred, the device plugin would report 0 allocatable slots on both eligible nodes.

Lower confidence — eval runner dependency on remote-agent-create: remote-agent-state calls createAgent internally (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905); if the create step is broken for any reason other than scheduling, state polling would also fail. However, the explicit scheduler message in all three checks points to scheduling as the common cause rather than an application-layer defect.

The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) is identical across all three checks, indicating the pod never reached a running state on any attempt. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"), so no existing pod could be evicted to free capacity. The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with type "remote" (line 1918), which triggers the pod submission that fails at the infrastructure layer before any application-level response is produced. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods and no preemption victims exist, so new remote-agent pods cannot be scheduled.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and making the cluster more sensitive to VM slot exhaustion.
Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval probe runs alongside production workloads.

Lower probability — a recent node or taint change that removed nodes from the eligible pool, shrinking capacity without a corresponding increase in VM slots on remaining nodes (no supporting evidence in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges).
